name: nav
title: Nav
description: The places a player can go from here: a control per destination, the one they are on marked, in four treatments from one component. `bar` is the foot of the screen, `tabs` a strip with a rule under the current one, `pills` a row of rounded controls, `drawer` a vertical list. Each destination rides on `data-gs-nav`, deliberately not `data-gs-choice` and not `data-gs-item`, so a test counting the options in a question never also counts a nav bar. `data-gs-active` is where the player is, which is not `data-gs-selected`, because a destination is not a pick they may reverse. Not available at all and available later stay two attributes because they render two ways: disabled goes flat and takes no focus, locked keeps its shape, shows a padlock and stays focusable and describable. Performs nothing: it does not navigate, change a route, or decide which destination is current.
docs: Pass `destinations`, one entry per place, each with an `id`, a `label` and an optional `icon`, which must be inline SVG taking `currentColor` so the theme owns its colour. Mark the current one with `active`; the component never works that out, because the host owns the route. Pass `presentation` and `placement` for the treatment and the edge it hugs. Pass `onNavigate`, which is called with the destination's id and nothing else. `disabled` and `locked` are separate: use `locked` for somewhere that opens later, which keeps its shape and its place in the tab order so a player can hear it described, and `disabled` for somewhere that is not coming back on this surface. Setting both leaves the destination disabled, because a control cannot be flat and keep its shape at once.
